title: β-Lactamases: Clav for A, Chelate for B
summary: Sort β-lactamases by Ambler class and the inhibitor that blocks them — ESBL, AmpC, KPC, metallo-β-lactamases and OXA-48 — detect carbapenemases with mCIM/eCIM, and avoid the aztreonam and hidden-penicillinase traps.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 58 Hit 5 (β-lactamase detection in staphylococci), Hit 9 (ESBL vs AmpC), Hit 10 (carbapenemase classes and inhibitors), Traps 1, 4 and 5. Checked against Dhavale 2026, Khan 2026, Jadhav 2026, Ferreira 2017 and Rapi 2026. Register flags: rv-mbl-aztreonam (Trap 5), rv-nitrocefin (Hit 5). Not taught: nitrocefin colour change and timing, KPC “boronic acid” inhibition (sources name avibactam, vaborbactam, relebactam), temocillin OXA-48 screen.

objectives: Explain how β-lactamases inactivate β-lactams and how inhibitors protect them.
Match ESBL, AmpC, KPC, MBL and OXA-48 enzymes to their Ambler class and inhibitor clue.
Recognise the aztreonam–MBL and hidden staphylococcal penicillinase traps.

scenes.title: Resistant to everything — or is it?
scenes.altText: A Klebsiella report: resistant to ceftriaxone, ceftazidime and meropenem. Three questions pop up: “Which enzyme?”, “Which inhibitor tells me?”, “Is any β-lactam still usable?” The mascot looks thoughtful.

cues.text: A Klebsiella from a blood culture is resistant to third-generation cephalosporins — and to meropenem.
Which enzyme is doing this? The answer changes treatment and infection control.
The clue is which inhibitor switches the enzyme off.

props.title: K. pneumoniae · blood
props.sub: Ceftriaxone R · ceftazidime R · meropenem R

scenes.title: Normal: how β-lactams and β-lactamases meet
scenes.altText: A β-lactam token (ring drawn as a square) binds penicillin-binding proteins in the cell wall and stops wall synthesis. A β-lactamase token approaches and opens the ring — the drug is inactivated. An inhibitor token (clavulanate) binds the β-lactamase first, protecting the drug. A table of Ambler classes appears: A (serine) — ESBL, KPC; B — metallo (zinc); C — AmpC; D — OXA.

cues.text: β-lactam drugs bind penicillin-binding proteins and stop the bacterial cell wall from being built.
β-lactamases are enzymes that open the β-lactam ring, inactivating the drug before it reaches its target.
A β-lactamase inhibitor binds the enzyme first and protects the drug — but each inhibitor only blocks certain enzymes.
So enzymes are grouped by the Ambler classes: A, C and D use serine; class B, the metallo-β-lactamases, need zinc.

scenes.title: What changes: match the enzyme to its inhibitor
scenes.altText: A five-row table appears row by row: class A ESBL — inhibited by clavulanate; class A KPC — inhibited by avibactam, vaborbactam, relebactam; class B MBL (NDM, VIM, IMP) — inhibited by EDTA, not by clavulanate or avibactam; class C AmpC — not inhibited by clavulanate, sulbactam or tazobactam (detected with cloxacillin/boronic acid disks; cefoxitin resistance is a low-specificity screen); class D OXA-48-like — inhibited by avibactam.

cues.text: ESBLs are class A enzymes that break down third-generation cephalosporins — and clavulanate inhibits them.
KPC is a class A carbapenemase. Newer inhibitors — avibactam, vaborbactam and relebactam — block it.
Metallo-β-lactamases, like NDM, VIM and IMP, need zinc. EDTA, a zinc chelator, inhibits them; clavulanate and avibactam don’t.
AmpC is class C. Clavulanate, sulbactam and tazobactam don’t inhibit it; labs detect it with cloxacillin or boronic acid disks, and cefoxitin resistance is a rough screen.
OXA-48-like enzymes are class D carbapenemases — avibactam inhibits them.

scenes.title: In the lab: mCIM, eCIM and hidden penicillinase
scenes.altText: mCIM: a meropenem disk is incubated in a suspension of the isolate, then placed on a lawn of susceptible E. coli ATCC 25922; if a carbapenemase destroyed the meropenem, the E. coli grows up to the disk (small zone) = carbapenemase. eCIM: the same test with EDTA added — if EDTA restores the zone, the carbapenemase is a metallo-β-lactamase. Second card: an MBL cannot hydrolyse aztreonam, but many MBL producers also carry ESBL or AmpC enzymes that do — so aztreonam alone often fails. Third card (staphylococci): a β-lactamase can hide behind a “susceptible” penicillin MIC; phenotypic tests differ in sensitivity — a negative nitrocefin test does not rule it out; the zone-edge test is more sensitive.

cues.text: The modified carbapenem inactivation method, mCIM: soak a meropenem disk in the isolate, then lay it on a lawn of susceptible E. coli. If the disk’s meropenem was destroyed, the E. coli grows right up to it — carbapenemase present.
The eCIM repeats this with EDTA. If EDTA restores the zone, the carbapenemase is a metallo-β-lactamase.
Metallo-β-lactamases can’t hydrolyse aztreonam — but many of these organisms also carry ESBL or AmpC enzymes that can. So aztreonam alone often fails, which is why it’s combined with avibactam.
In staphylococci, penicillinase can hide behind a susceptible penicillin result. Tests differ: a negative nitrocefin test doesn’t rule it out, and the zone-edge test is more sensitive.

props.title: Staphylococcal penicillinase
lines: Can hide behind a susceptible penicillin MIC
Negative nitrocefin ≠ excluded · zone-edge test more sensitive

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Trap card: “Clavulanate inhibits AmpC” is crossed out → “Clavulanate inhibits ESBL, not AmpC.” Trap card: “Ceftazidime–avibactam covers NDM” is crossed out → “Avibactam doesn’t inhibit metallo-β-lactamases.” Trap card: “MBL can’t hydrolyse aztreonam, so aztreonam alone always works” is crossed out → “Co-produced ESBL/AmpC often inactivate it.”

cues.text: Trap one: clavulanate inhibits ESBLs — not AmpC.
Trap two: avibactam doesn’t inhibit metallo-β-lactamases, so ceftazidime–avibactam lacks activity against NDM producers.
Trap three: aztreonam survives metallo-β-lactamases, but co-produced ESBL or AmpC enzymes often destroy it — so don’t assume aztreonam alone will work.

scenes.title: Clav for A, chelate for B
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Clav for A (ESBL), chelate for B (MBL), C ignores clav, and avibactam guards A and D.” A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: clav for A, chelate for B. C ignores clav. And avibactam guards A and D.

Where it breaks: some class A enzymes are carbapenemases that clavulanate doesn’t reliably block; isolates often carry several enzymes at once; inhibitor tests can give false positives; and treatment follows current breakpoints and guidance, not the enzyme name alone.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “ESBL–clavulanate · KPC/OXA-48–avibactam · MBL–EDTA (not avibactam) · AmpC–not clavulanate”, “mCIM finds carbapenemase; eCIM (EDTA) flags MBL · aztreonam vs MBL only if no ESBL/AmpC”.

cues.text: Identify β-lactamases by which inhibitor stops them — clavulanate for ESBL, avibactam for KPC and OXA-48, EDTA for metallo-enzymes — and confirm carbapenemases with mCIM and eCIM.

props.label: mCIM: carbapenemase · eCIM (EDTA): MBL · watch co-produced enzymes

explanation.what: Plain language: bacteria make enzymes that break β-lactam drugs, and the drug that blocks each enzyme is the clue to which one it is. Scientific terms: Ambler classes A (ESBL, KPC), B (metallo-β-lactamases: NDM, VIM, IMP; zinc-dependent), C (AmpC), D (OXA, incl. OXA-48-like). ESBL inhibited by clavulanate; AmpC not inhibited by clavulanate, sulbactam, tazobactam; KPC inhibited by avibactam, vaborbactam, relebactam; MBL inhibited by EDTA, not by clavulanate or avibactam; OXA-48 by avibactam.
explanation.why: Serine β-lactamases (A, C, D) and zinc-dependent MBLs (B) differ chemically, so inhibitors work selectively. MBLs cannot hydrolyse aztreonam, but co-produced ESBL/AmpC enzymes can.
explanation.measure: mCIM: meropenem disk incubated with the isolate, placed on E. coli ATCC 25922 lawn — small/no zone = carbapenemase; eCIM (EDTA) restores the zone for MBL producers (CLSI-standardised). AmpC disk tests with cloxacillin/boronic acid; cefoxitin resistance is a low-specificity screen. Staphylococcal penicillinase: combined phenotypic tests; zone-edge more sensitive than nitrocefin.
explanation.differs: ESBL vs AmpC (clavulanate), KPC/OXA-48 vs MBL (avibactam vs EDTA), carbapenemase-producing vs non-producing CRE.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: enzyme–inhibitor matching, mCIM/eCIM interpretation, aztreonam and MBL, AmpC detection, hidden staphylococcal β-lactamase.

comparisons.title: ESBL vs AmpC
comparisons.distinguisher: Clavulanate effect; cloxacillin/boronic acid disks for AmpC.

comparisons.title: KPC vs metallo-β-lactamase
comparisons.distinguisher: eCIM: EDTA restores the zone only for MBL.

mnemonic.text: Clav for A, chelate for B; C ignores clav; avibactam guards A and D.
mnemonic.explanation: Clavulanate inhibits class A ESBLs; EDTA chelates zinc in class B MBLs; AmpC resists clavulanate; avibactam inhibits KPC and OXA-48.
mnemonic.limitation: KPC is class A but needs newer inhibitors; isolates often carry several enzymes; treatment follows current breakpoints and guidance.

analogyLimitations: Plates, zones and tokens are schematic; zone sizes are not CLSI criteria.
Detailed CLSI zone criteria, molecular assays and treatment choices are not covered.
takeaway: Identify β-lactamases by which inhibitor stops them — clavulanate for ESBL, avibactam for KPC and OXA-48, EDTA for metallo-enzymes — and confirm carbapenemases with mCIM and eCIM.

questions.stem: A meropenem-resistant K. pneumoniae is mCIM positive. In the eCIM, adding EDTA restores the meropenem zone. Which enzyme is most likely?

options.rationale: Correct. EDTA chelates zinc and inhibits MBLs, restoring the zone.
Incorrect. KPC is a serine enzyme not inhibited by EDTA.
Incorrect. OXA-48 is a serine (class D) enzyme.
Incorrect. A positive mCIM indicates carbapenemase activity.

questions.stem: An E. cloacae isolate is resistant to cefoxitin and ceftazidime, and adding clavulanate does not restore ceftazidime activity; a cloxacillin disk does. Which enzyme fits?

options.rationale: Correct. AmpC is not inhibited by clavulanate but is by cloxacillin/boronic acid.
Incorrect. ESBLs are inhibited by clavulanate.
Incorrect. MBLs are inhibited by EDTA, and the isolate is not described as carbapenem-resistant.
Incorrect. blaZ is a staphylococcal penicillinase.

questions.stem: Which statement about ceftazidime–avibactam is correct?

options.text: It is active against KPC and OXA-48 producers but lacks activity against MBL producers
options.rationale: Correct. Avibactam inhibits serine enzymes, not zinc-dependent MBLs.
Incorrect. Avibactam does not inhibit MBLs.

options.text: It is inactive against KPC producers

options.rationale: Incorrect. EDTA is a laboratory chelator, not part of the drug.

references.citation: Dhavale SL, Patil HV, Patil SR. Carbapenemase detection methods in clinical microbiology: conventional and automated approaches. Cureus. 2026;18(7):e112242.
references.usedFor: Ambler classes: class A KPC, class B MBLs (NDM, VIM, IMP), class D OXA-48-like; MBLs zinc-dependent, inhibited by EDTA, resistant to common inhibitors, cannot hydrolyse aztreonam; CLSI-standardised mCIM/eCIM — meropenem disk incubated with isolate, placed on E. coli ATCC 25922 lawn; eCIM uses EDTA to inhibit MBLs.

references.citation: Khan M, Patil P, Rathored J. Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative pathogens: molecular epidemiology, diagnostic advances, and emerging therapeutic strategies. Front Microbiol. 2026;17:1913726.
references.usedFor: Avibactam, vaborbactam and relebactam inhibit KPC; ceftazidime–avibactam active against KPC and OXA-48 producers, lacks activity against MBL producers; aztreonam resists MBL hydrolysis but co-expressed ESBL/AmpC inactivate it, hence aztreonam combinations.

references.citation: Jadhav PS, Mane PM, Patil S. AmpC β-lactamases in SPICE organisms: a rising threat to antimicrobial therapy. Cureus. 2026;18(5):e109750.
references.usedFor: AmpC (class C) hydrolyses cephamycins (cefoxitin) and extended-spectrum cephalosporins; not inhibited by clavulanate, sulbactam or tazobactam (unlike ESBLs); detection: cefoxitin screen (low specificity), AmpC disk tests with cloxacillin/boronic acid; MBLs inhibited by EDTA not clavulanate.

references.citation: Ferreira AM, Martins KB, Silva VR, Mondelli AL, Cunha ML. Correlation of phenotypic tests with the presence of the blaZ gene for detection of beta-lactamase. Braz J Microbiol. 2017;48(1):159-166.
references.usedFor: In staphylococci (S. saprophyticus study): zone-edge test most sensitive (90.3%), nitrocefin least sensitive (28.9%) for blaZ; combined tests improve accuracy; penicillin susceptibility defined with a negative chromogenic cephalosporin (nitrocefin) test; penicillinase inactivates penicillin by hydrolysing the β-lactam ring; nitrocefin changes colour when its β-lactam ring is opened.

references.citation: Rapi MC, Filipe J, Penati M, et al. Phenotypic resistance to life-saving antimicrobials in Gram-positive bacteria isolated from wild birds in Northern Italy: a One Health surveillance perspective. One Health. 2026;23:101551.
references.usedFor: β-lactams act by binding penicillin-binding proteins (low-affinity PBP5 reduces β-lactam binding and confers resistance in E. faecium).

claims.text: Ambler A (ESBL, KPC), B (MBL; zinc), C (AmpC), D (OXA-48-like).
ESBL–clavulanate; AmpC not inhibited by clavulanate/sulbactam/tazobactam; KPC–avibactam/vaborbactam/relebactam; MBL–EDTA not avibactam; OXA-48–avibactam.
mCIM detects carbapenemase; eCIM (EDTA) identifies MBL (CLSI-standardised).
MBLs can’t hydrolyse aztreonam; co-produced ESBL/AmpC can.
AmpC detection: cloxacillin/boronic acid disks; cefoxitin screen low specificity.
Staphylococcal penicillinase can be missed; nitrocefin less sensitive than zone-edge test.
β-lactams bind PBPs; β-lactamases hydrolyse the β-lactam ring; nitrocefin changes colour when its ring is opened.
